title: On the Divergence of Differential Temporal Difference Learning without Local Clocks
claim: A conjugate eigenvalue pair of the system matrix crosses into the right half-plane over a bounded parameter interval, producing instability.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, complex-plane trajectory beside real-part curve with shaded unstable band
description: Two side-by-side matplotlib plots in blue on white. The left panel, "Conjugate-pair trajectory", plots Re(λ) against Im(λ) for a complex-conjugate pair of eigenvalues. Two mirrored blue curves start at open circles near Re=1.5 (η≈0) and sweep left toward the imaginary axis. Arrows show the direction of travel. Black dots mark η=ε, 3ε and the crossing points on the axis, and squares mark η=4ε. A grey band covers the left half-plane. The right panel, "Real part of crossing pair", plots Re(λ) against t=η/ε. The curve falls steeply from 1.5, dips slightly below zero, then rises again. Dotted vertical lines at t=1 and t=3 bound a grey "unstable" interval. A black dot at η=2ε marks the minimum. The eye goes first to the blue curves and the shaded region.
caption: Phase portrait of the nontrivial eigenvalues of $A_\eta/\varepsilon$ for the counterexample in Example [ref]. Left: trajectory of the conjugate pair in the complex plane. Right: real part of this pair as a function of $t=\eta/\varepsilon$, with the unstable interval $t\in(1,3)$ shaded.
abstract: Learning rate is a critical component of reinforcement learning (RL). This work uses global and local clocks to distinguish two types of learning rates. The former is of the standard form $Î±_t$ that depends only on the time step $t$ (i.e., a global clock). The latter is of the form $Î±_{Î½(S_t, t)}$, where $Î½(s, t)$ counts the number of visits to state $s$ until time $t$ (i.e., a local clock). In discounted RL, an RL algorithm that is convergent with a local clock is always also convergent with a global clock, and vice versa. We are not aware of any counterexample. The key contribution of this work is to show that this nice correspondence breaks down in average-reward RL. Specifically, we construct a counterexample showing that although differential temporal difference (TD) learning is convergent with a local clock, it can diverge with a global clock. We empirically observe this divergence in our experiments and also prove that the associated ODE of differential TD with a global clock is unstable. This counterexample closes the open problem in Wan et al. [2021], Blaser et al. [2026].
